source.title: The large learning rate phase of deep learning: the catapult mechanism
source.authors: Aitor Lewkowycz; Yasaman Bahri; Ethan Dyer; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein; Guy Gur-Ari

record.tranche_reason: Tests how learning rate changes test performance and curvature in trained networks, using outcomes different from the claim versions' specified interventions and measures.
record.gate_note: The study tests learning-rate regimes and reports training dynamics, curvature, and test accuracy. It does not test the listed versions. Values visible only in plots are recorded as figure only; cited results from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own learning-rate and curvature results, but none tests V1–V8. Its closest connection is V7: top NTK eigenvalue is an unscaled local curvature measure, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, and the study does not compare rankings against norm- or margin-based measures. Different fixed batch sizes across architectures do not constitute a V5 batch-size comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors identify catapult dynamics that reduce curvature and permit stable training above the linearized model's critical learning rate. They report that catapult-phase performance matches or exceeds lazy-phase performance in their comparisons, with the best fixed-compute results in the catapult phase. They also explicitly report a fixed-physical-time CNN setting where curvature does not correlate with test performance. These conclusions concern MSE-based experiments and do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness claim.
record.recipe_differences: Studies learning-rate regimes rather than the versions' interventions; uses MSE loss and SGD in the reported experiments, with varying architectures, datasets, regularization, and compute schedules.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate; fixed-step versus fixed-physical-time budget; learning-rate decay; L2 regularization; architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Catapult-phase learning rates produce the best fixed-step performance in the tested settings. With physical time controlled, advantages depend on architecture, learning-rate decay, and regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large initial learning rates in the catapult phase can improve generalization, with the advantage depending on the training budget and recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: For the CIFAR-10 CNN at fixed physical time, test performance remains essentially flat across learning rates despite changes in top NTK eigenvalue; the authors explicitly report no curvature–performance correlation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled top NTK eigenvalue does not consistently track held-out accuracy across learning-rate settings.

record.problems: One initialization is generally used for comparisons. Learning rates and L2 regularization were not hyperparameter tuned for the Wide ResNet experiments. Many accuracy values are shown only in figures without exact text values; the authors state that precision aspects of curvature fluctuations were not a focus.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Test-error trends as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold. The supplementary width sweep measures kernel changes, not this test-error trend.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size sweeps under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout additions, removal, configuration, and interaction with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their association with generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equal-size random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures do not instantiate those versions; this does not mean the study's qualitative learning-rate findings are unreadable. No additional results bearing directly on a listed version were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and held-out accuracy on random labels.
A width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error and the resulting test-error trend.
A comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks, including local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and comparing with random removals.

rows.subject: fully-connected 1 hidden layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Compared final train and test accuracy across learning rates after full-batch gradient descent on 512 MNIST samples.

conditions.value: until training accuracy reaches 1 or 700k physical steps

rows.measure: Final train accuracy and test accuracy
rows.note: The text says optimal performance is above the critical learning rate and close to the expected maximum, but gives no exact test-accuracy values.
rows.check: The learning-rate comparison is valid but measures no listed version. Its qualitative outcome is readable from the text: optimal test performance occurs in the catapult phase; exact accuracy values are not supplied.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy across initial learning rates under fixed-step and fixed-physical-time schedules.
rows.note: Text reports a significant small-versus-large learning-rate performance gap for fixed steps; at fixed physical time performance is flat up to the maximum learning rate and curvature does not correlate with generalization.
rows.check: The original partial state has no applicable claim version. Split fixed-step training in Figure 5a from fixed-physical-time training in Figure 5b: the former favors larger learning rates, whereas the latter has essentially flat performance despite differing curvature. Figure 5a uses no decay; Figure 5b includes both decay and no-decay conditions.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy across initial learning rates under fixed-step and fixed-physical-time schedules.
rows.note: Text reports a significant performance gap for fixed steps and says optimal performance is above the critical learning rate under fixed physical time.
rows.check: The original observed state has no applicable claim version. Separate fixed-step, no-decay results in Figure 5c from fixed-physical-time results with and without decay in Figure 5d. These are learning-rate comparisons, not batch-size or width comparisons.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy across initial learning rates, with and without learning-rate decay.

conditions.value: fixed steps; fixed physical time with decay

rows.note: The text says that after decay at the same physical epoch, larger learning rates do better.
rows.check: The original observed state has no applicable claim version. Split fixed-step training in Figure S2a from fixed-physical-time training with and without decay in Figure S2b. The stated larger-learning-rate advantage after decay applies specifically to the latter comparison.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared learning-rate performance with a larger L2 regularization value.
rows.note: Authors say optimal performance in physical time is still peaked in the catapult phase, but the difference is smaller.
rows.check: The original partial state describes a weaker learning-rate advantage, not an incomplete effect under any listed version. Figure S5 includes distinct fixed-step and fixed-physical-time conditions that should be separate rows.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy across learning rates without L2 regularization.
rows.note: Authors state that larger learning rates do better without L2 regularization, even without learning-rate decay; training takes a long time.
rows.check: The original observed state has no applicable claim version. Figure S4 compares learning rates 0.2 and 0.02 over physical epochs without L2 or learning-rate decay; it does not test dropout removal or any other listed intervention.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
